Generated-video rows are scored from automatic labels: two independent annotators must give the same answer, and a label they do not settle counts as a failure (0 certified, 71 agreed but uncertified, 89 unresolved scored fields). retained_failures.what: S02 v1 native run 1 (runner job 3606570, gh151)

Kept failed and not rerun; scene and contract version 2 are two blocks shorter so that the route stays inside the starting chunk.

notes: The route is scripted (keys held for fixed numbers of steps); Minecraft's own movement and collision decide where the player ends. This shows that the goal is reached around the wall and not through it. Nothing here plans a route: no P system has been run.

The camera is the player's view and moves with the player. The player's place is read back from the engine (region predicates, with x and z in hundredths of a block beside them); it is not bound to recorded frames.

Version 2 of the scene. Version 1 was two blocks longer; its advance crossed a chunk border of the world and the recording's clock check failed four steps later (run 1, a retained failure). Version 2 keeps the whole route inside the starting chunk.
One wall and one goal: a closed room (no route at all), a longer detour and a moving obstacle are not tested.

retained_failures.what: S05 v1 native run 1 (runner job 3606570, gh151)
retained_failures.reason: stopped at the baseline read in both branches ('Absent or unknown S05 native fields'): the command that resets the read storage was 316 characters long and the chat cut it at 256, so the engine rejected it. Kept failed; the module now uses short storage keys and checks the length.

retained_failures.what: S05 v1 native run 2 (runner job 3606570, gh151)
retained_failures.reason: branch A failed at after_recipe: the coal had moved and the furnace was lit, but the ore was unchanged 242 game ticks after the activation. A furnace created by command stores no cook-time total and never finishes an item. Kept failed; the scene now writes the recipe's 200 ticks into both furnaces. Branch B passed and is not used.

notes: The recipe is Minecraft's own smelting in a furnace, not a recipe of the crafting grid: the grid needs the inventory screen, which the scenario does not drive. The engine moves one coal from the supply (a dropper that faces the furnace's fuel side, activated once by a redstone block placed under it), burns it, consumes the ore and makes the ingot.

Both furnaces are created by command with the recipe's cooking time (200 ticks) written into them. A furnace created by command without it never finishes an item; the engine writes that value itself when an item is put in by hand or by a hopper. Run 2 failed for lack of it.

One coal burns for 1600 ticks and one ore needs 200: the furnace is still lit at both later checkpoints and the rest of the burn time is lost. Two ores, a missing ingredient and a full output slot are not tested.

Contents are not visible in the picture; the furnace's fire is. The counts are derived from native block predicates (each slot with evidence for the occupied and for the empty side) and a block-data read of the supply; they are not bound to recorded frames.

Third engine run of this scene. Run 1 stopped at the first read (the command that resets the read storage was longer than the chat limit of 256 characters) and run 2 at the second checkpoint (see above); both are retained failures of the scenario module, not of the engine.
Run as a bare driver inside the runner's allocation (job 3606570, gh151): there is no worker receipt. Command, exit code and logs are beside the output (artifacts/s05-20261115/native-run-3.*).

validation.truth_source: known by construction (native state of the frame the baseline replays)
notes: Baseline frames are native frames; most are also reference frames of the full reader (in-sample), except replayed first frames.
Predictions and margins only; readable_rate counts reader answers, including streams voided by the sanity anchor as unreadable.

limits: Native leave-one-frame-out (near-duplicate frames stay in the references): changed state 19 of 19 answers correct, out of 21 reads (2 not evaluable, 0 unreadable); unchanged state 45 of 45 answers correct, out of 46 reads (0 not evaluable, 1 unreadable).

Native leave-one-branch-out (separate engine executions): changed state 7 of 7 answers correct, out of 20 reads (11 not evaluable, 2 unreadable); unchanged state 31 of 31 answers correct, out of 44 reads (12 not evaluable, 1 unreadable).
All native validation uses one scene and one fixed camera per task. It shows that a region and its centroids separate the two native appearances; it says nothing about generated frames.
Uncalibrated: no human labels exist; generated-domain accuracy is unknown.
One native run per task supplies the reference frames; n is tiny and frames within a run are correlated. No interval.
Fields with identical native truth patterns that are not given a region of their own are covered by one representative field; the reader cannot separate them.

A projected region is the image of a named cell or entity box under the task's fixed camera (pinhole, 70 degree vertical field of view, checked against native overlays). It is fixed in the image: a stream that moves the camera is read at the wrong place.
Thresholds fixed a priori (margin 0.10, far factor 1.0); never tuned on generated frames.

S07/target_present: accepted - Region is the target cell immediately to the viewer's left of the blue marker: the gold block fills it before the delete, floor and wall show after it. The identical gold block on the right is outside.
S10/landing_sand: accepted - Region is the landing cell on the floor to the viewer's left of the blue cube: empty floor before the fall, filled by the landed sand block after it.

S10/source_sand: accepted_with_limit - Region is the source cell high on the column. Its bounding rectangle also holds about 14 pixel rows of the support block's front face under the sand, because the far lower edge of a cell projects below its near lower edge.
S10/support_present: accepted - Region is the support cell: the stone block's front face and underside. Its top row touches the lower edge of the sand block.

S12/target_lower_open: accepted_with_limit - Region is the image of the closed target door's slab. Closed, the door fills it; open, it shows the wall behind and the edge of the swung slab. The powered cell under the door begins at the region's bottom edge (at most 2 pixel rows overlap). Limit on generated frames: at EdenLive after_L3 (branch A) and after_L2 and after_L3 (branch B) the reviewer sees the door swung open, but the patch matches neither native appearance (the generated open door is drawn thicker and a small bright artefact sits in the doorway), so the reader returns unreadable and the protocol counts that as a failure. Those S12 rows are a probable reader miss until human labels exist.
S14/near_red: accepted - Region is the near eligible cube at the far left of the view: its front and top faces fill it.
S14/far_red: accepted - Region is the leftmost cube of the rear row; the protected cube to its right and the near cube to its left are outside.

S22/target_color: accepted_with_limit - Region is the target sheep's hitbox: head, body, legs and the floor at its feet; the neighbouring sheep, the blue cube and the held shears are outside. Dropped wool can fall inside its left and lower edge. Not scored where the sheep is sheared.

S22/target_sheared: accepted_with_limit - Same region as target_color. Fleeced and sheared differ in body bulk and leg exposure, which is small next to fleece colour and dropped wool. Native leave-one-branch-out reads 2 of 4 sheared frames, with the other 2 unreadable and none wrong. On the EdenLive after_shear frames the reader returns unreadable, and the reviewer cannot tell the fleece state there either.

readers.kind: deterministic camera-pose reader for a scene of known geometry: frame 0 is aligned to each frame through the scene's voxel model (dense, normalised cross-correlation); tracked corners with RANSAC PnP check it

validation.truth_source: construction: the clip is one native frame shown for its whole length, so the camera neither moves nor turns
notes: clips: baseline-frozen-first-frame/S01-v1/single
largest read motion against frame 0: 0.0002 blocks, 0.0021 degrees
The held frames are exact copies, so this shows that the reader and the scoring fail a clip without motion; it says nothing about a nearly still generated clip with noise.

validation.truth_source: engine player pose logged for every recorded frame (states.jsonl); motion of each frame against frame 0, read by the same nearest-class rule on both sides
notes: clips: native-oracle/S01-v1/single, native-oracle/S12-v1/A, native-oracle/S12-v1/B
class boundaries at half of 1.073 blocks and 25.0 degrees (the moving clip's own motion)
position error against the engine pose of the same step, blocks: mean 0.018, max 0.209
position error against the engine pose one step earlier, blocks: mean 0.012, max 0.074
yaw error, degrees: mean 0.038, max 0.932; pitch error, degrees: mean 0.018, max 0.130

A recorded frame shows the position of the previous engine step and the rotation of the current one, so the position error against the same step is the larger of the two while the camera moves. A frame near a class boundary can therefore read one class behind the engine.

limits: Uncalibrated against people: no human has labelled camera motion in any clip. The annotation packet asks 16 camera-motion questions about generated clips; none is answered yet.
Validated on native clips of one room only (the S01 move-and-turn clip and the static S12 clips); no native clip with a left turn, a pitch change or sideways motion has been read.
The pose is camera motion relative to frame 0 under the scenario's geometry and first pose. The reader does not test that frame 0 shows that scene.
Classes are decided at half the engine's own motion in the commanded phase (nearest class). Smaller errors of amount are reported as numbers, not scored.
Sky, distant terrain, levers, open doors and the HUD are not used; a scene made mostly of those cannot be read. Roll is assumed zero by the first estimator.
Where the second estimator has no answer the first stands alone; the checkpoint says so.

Constants were revised after a first version returned a wrong pose on the EdenLive S01 clip; the history is in the reader's module text and the dev runs are kept. No constant was chosen against an expected generated answer.

metrics.name: Checkpoint success
metrics.formula: passed scored checkpoints / scored checkpoints (pass, fail, unreadable) over both branches of one task instance
metrics.aggregation: task value; category macro = equal-weight mean over scored categories
metrics.unsupported_policy: excluded, unsupported and missing checkpoints leave the denominator and are reported

metrics.name: Branch success
metrics.formula: branches whose every scored checkpoint passed / branches with at least one scored checkpoint
metrics.aggregation: task value; category macro = equal-weight mean
metrics.unsupported_policy: excluded, unsupported and missing checkpoints leave the denominator and are reported

metrics.name: Strict pair success (S_pair)
metrics.formula: 1 if both branches of a paired instance succeed, else 0 (product over both branches and all scored checkpoints)
metrics.aggregation: task value; category macro over paired categories
metrics.unsupported_policy: excluded, unsupported and missing checkpoints leave the denominator and are reported

metrics.name: Readable rate
metrics.formula: readable fields / oracle-visible fields over scored checkpoints
metrics.aggregation: task value; category macro = equal-weight mean
metrics.unsupported_policy: excluded, unsupported and missing checkpoints leave the denominator and are reported

metrics.name: Target-field accuracy
metrics.unsupported_policy: excluded, unsupported and missing checkpoints leave the denominator and are reported

metrics.name: Imaging quality (MUSIQ/100)
metrics.formula: VBench imaging_quality (pyiqa MUSIQ) per video; mean within branch; equal-branch mean within category; /100
metrics.aggregation: equal-weight mean over measured categories, per domain
metrics.unsupported_policy: unmeasured categories are rows with value null

glossary.text: Produced by an actual engine or model run retained on disk.
Produced on a synthetic or reference-DSL fixture; tests the pipeline, not a Minecraft or model capability.
An existing benchmark metric applied outside its official protocol.
An official benchmark protocol result. None exists here.
The native engine read against its own expected states: an upper-bound diagnostic of the measurement, never a model score.

Scored from automatic labels (ADR 0013, 0014): two independent annotators answered the same blind question about the picture and gave the same answer. 'Uncertified' means at least one label rests on annotators whose known-answer sets are too small to show 95 % reliability. A label the annotators do not settle is unresolved and counts as a failure. Never a human label.

Pictures whose answer is known without a person: native frames with the engine state, the same frames in the generated picture format (blurred, compressed, resampled), composites with the region from another state, and occluded regions where the right answer is 'cannot tell'. Pictures made from one native frame form one cluster.
Scored by a reader that has not been calibrated against human labels.
A degenerate baseline that validates the metrics (proposal 9.3).
Scored from system-produced or engine-read state, not from pixels.
A replay of retained media; not live.
Switching between pre-recorded branches; not live.
A live system answering one turn at a time.
A live system streaming frames continuously.
Every scored field matches the expected state.
At least one scored field is wrong, or the output is missing.
The oracle is readable but the output is not; counts as a failure.
The system or baseline does not apply to this case.
The oracle itself is not visible here; not scored.
No observation exists to read (no frame, or no reader for the state class); not scored.

limits: 0 human labels. An automatic label is not a human label.

No annotator is certified for any field class: the known-answer sets have 2 to 9 decided clusters per annotator and class, and certification needs at least 59 error-free clusters. More native executions per field class are what would change this.

Known-answer pictures and clips are native frames and transforms of them. None comes out of a generator (the autoencoder round trip is not built), so a failure that only generated pictures provoke is not measured.

An annotator that made a known-answer error in a class is not used for that class (vlm-cosmosreason1-7b-v1: camera_rotation, camera_translation, cube_material, iron_door_open, sheep_fleece_colour, sheep_fleece_state, source_cell_sand, support_block_presence, target_block_presence; vlm-qwen3vl8b-v1: camera_rotation, camera_translation, iron_door_open, sheep_fleece_state, source_cell_sand, support_block_presence; vlm-qwen3vl8b-zoom-v1: cube_material, iron_door_open, sheep_fleece_state, source_cell_sand, support_block_presence). Where that leaves fewer than two independent annotators, labels of the class are unresolved and count as failures. That lowers a score for a reason that lies with the labelling, not the system; each row shows its resolved-only value beside it. Classes left without two: camera_rotation, camera_translation, iron_door_open, sheep_fleece_state, source_cell_sand, support_block_presence.

Camera motion (ADR 0016): the known-answer clips come from three native recordings in one room, four clusters per class (a forward move, a right turn and two still recordings). A left turn exists only as a mirrored or reversed right turn, a move other than forward only as a reversed forward move, and no clip changes pitch, so 'turns another way' is never tested. The pose reader is judged on the native pictures only.

Annotators of one independence group are one mechanism and never count as two. With more annotators there are more chances that one is free of errors on a small known-answer set by luck; every annotator's result is in the tables, used or not.
